note: Regenerated deliberately with tools/check_rules.py --update. Every rule whose hash changed had its citations reviewed at that moment.

0.title: The rules are read at the start of every task

1.1.title: Design before code — a gate, not a preference (owner requirement, 2026-09-24)

1.2.title: Design from the product, not from the code that exists (owner requirement, 2026-09-24)

1.10.title: A plan is attacked before anything is built from it (owner requirement, 2026-09-25)

4.1.title: A child row carries its tenant into its foreign key (added 2026-09-26, finding J3)

5.title: Security and authentication, from each module's first commit

5.1.title: Staff and administrator accounts — the higher bar (owner requirement, 2026-09-23)

9.title: A module is complete only when someone else has attacked it

16.title: How work is delegated to agents (owner requirement)

16.1.title: Every agent reads the rules first

16.2.title: The minimum capable model, and one hard thing at a time

16.3.title: An agent's silence is never a pass

16.4.title: What an agent's report is worth

16.5.title: The delegation decision is declared, not assumed

16.6.title: What the agents actually got wrong, and what that changes (2026-09-24)

17.title: Where we are weak, stated plainly

18.title: Every service we depend on is recorded, with the reason (owner requirement)

19.title: The brief is the plan of record, and it is kept true (owner requirement)

20.title: The public site, and what we say on it (owner requirement)

21.title: A control states the coverage it has, in the tool's own words (added 2026-09-24)

21.1.title:
A control's stated scope is quoted from what the tool reports, never from what it was meant
to do

21.2.title: A new control ships having fired at least once, on purpose

21.3.title: Every batch closes with a coverage line, in the same place as the 16.5 declaration

21.4.title: "What this does not prove" is required of every control, not only of tests

21.5.title: A remediation claim quotes the authority that decides it

21.6.title: One sample is not a pattern

21.7.title: An exit code is not evidence of an effect

21.8.title: A cited file, path or symbol must exist (added 2026-09-26)

21.9.title:
A guard patched twice for the same class is replaced, not patched a third time (added
2026-09-26)

22.title: A scripted edit is verified mechanically, not by eye (added 2026-09-24)

22.1.title: An anchored edit asserts its anchor is unique before it writes

22.2.title: Every scripted edit to a structured file is followed by a parse of the result

22.3.title: Prose passed to a tool goes through a file, never inline

23.title: Changing a rule is a change to everything that cites it (added 2026-09-25)

23.1.title: Sub-rule numbers are explicit, and new sub-rules are appended, never inserted

23.2.title: A retired rule keeps its number and is tombstoned in place

23.3.title:
A rule's text and title are recorded in `docs/rules-manifest.json`, and changing either fails
the build until the citations have been reviewed

23.4.title: Renaming or rewording a rule carries the same obligation as renumbering it

23.5.title: The plan of record is updated in the same change as the rule

24.title: Every mistake is written down, and answered with a mechanism (added 2026-09-25)

24.1.title: Every defect found in our own work gets an entry

24.2.title:
Every entry names the rule that now prevents recurrence — or says plainly that none does, and
why

24.3.title: A rule written in response lands in the same change as the ledger entry

24.4.title: A repeat is treated as evidence that the first rule was decorative

24.5.title: The test for any new rule: would it have caught this mechanically?

24.6.title:
A finding is not "closed" until the claim cites every document the finding named — and a fix is
not proved until someone else has checked it (added 2026-09-25)
